text:
Kai: quick dump from a short perf sweep on the long-sequence (≈1k tokens) workload. captured end-to-end p95/p99 and broken down by prefill vs decode. attaching summary below.

Ana: drop the hotspots please :eyes:

Kai: summary (abbrev):
```
prefill:  520ms matmul-heavy + 95ms kv_lookup
decode:   260ms cross_attn + 410ms kv_miss_path
mb=12 -> throughput +18% but p99 increases ~1.6x
mb=3  -> p95 stable, p99 decreases ~40% but throughput -30%
```

Mike: hm. looks like KV miss amplification during decode. are misses because prefill touched different prefix layouts? streaming long context could be evicting hot entries.

Sophia: validated on a couple runs: enabling split-prefill (prefill split into smaller kernel passes) dropped kv hit-rate from ~95% -> ~74%. that aligns with higher kv_miss_path cost during decode.

Jess: so tradeoff is microbatch sizing vs tail. any low-risk wins besides shrinking batches? we can't slow throughput much.

Kai: a few ideas from the trace: 1) kernel switch overhead is nontrivial. current policy flips kernel at seq_len>128 and we end up toggling mid-request for many streams. each switch (context memcpy + launch) is 30-55ms. propose increasing threshold to 192 and adding hysteresis (require delta >64 tokens before switching back).
2) decouple prefill kernel from decode kernel when memory layout allows: keep prefill on throughput kernel, but reuse buffer layout so decode kernel can be used without a heavy copy.
3) KV strategy: promote recent prefixes to an L1 in-host cache with a short pin window (e.g., 10s) when host memory pressure < 70%. this reduces disk-backed misses on busy streaming paths.
4) add SLO-aware batching: route-level hints to cap batch size for latency-sensitive traffic and permit large batches for background/off-peak tiers.

Ana: hysteresis + decoupled kernel choice sounds promising. we should be careful around memory aliasing when reusing buffers between kernels.

Mike: curious about quantization path churn. are we switching kernels due to int8 vs fp16 decisions too often?

Kai: in these runs quant paths were static. main cost was kv_miss + splitpoint copy. linked a pprof snapshot in CI (mock link): https://ci.internal/redwood/prof/1864007890/pprof

Sophia: experiment idea: for very long incoming sequences, do a fast first-pass prefill for the initial ~512 tokens on throughput kernel to get initial kv priming, then switch to smaller decode-friendly batches. that amortizes kernel init while keeping tail-friendly decode.

Jess: can we implement SLO hints now? route config could include slo_ms and prefer_low_latency flag; batcher uses that to pick min/max batch. example: 
```
route:
  slo_ms: 160
  prefer_low_latency: true
  batching:
    min_batch: 1
    max_batch: 6
```
Wire that into continuous-batcher.

Mike: ok actions we agreed on:
1) Kai: PR for kernel-switch hysteresis + threshold bump, include perf job.
2) Sophia: prototype split-prefill (512 fast pass + decode chunks) and run sims.
3) Jess: expose per-route SLO hints to the batcher and add policy mapping.
4) Ana: prototype in-host KV hot-promotion with simple TTL and memory-pressure gating.

Jess: will run a canary on dedicated-staging after PRs. goal: reduce p99 without losing >15% throughput.

deploy-bot: canary scheduled on dedicated-staging at 2028-10-02T09:00:00Z (job id: cb-18640078)

Kai: thanks folks. I'll open the PRs and post follow-up perf runs here. short take: prioritize kernel hysteresis + SLO-aware batching as quickest path to p99 wins with minimal throughput impact.
